claim_text: LALIGA says it was the target of a cyberattack on a fan-services platform
summary: LALIGA's own statement says it suffered a cyberattack aimed at one of its technology platforms for fan services.
detail: The statement is on LALIGA's own website. Reuters (via CNA) and Europa Press report the same statement, so the three count as one source.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's statement says in its own words that it suffered a cyberattack.
notes: Company statement, Tier 1. The two outlets relay it.

claim_text: LALIGA says personal data of registered users was extracted
summary: LALIGA says an attacker extracted personal data of users registered in digital services of LALIGA and of some clubs.
detail: The statement says 'extrajeron datos personales'. It does not say which kinds of personal data. Reuters adds that the extent is yet to be determined.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's statement says personal data was extracted.
notes: Company statement, Tier 1. The two outlets relay it.

claim_text: LALIGA says the attacker had access from Nov 14 to 16 and was blocked on Nov 16
summary: LALIGA says an attacker accessed the platform illegitimately between Nov 14 and 16. On Nov 16 its security teams applied measures to contain the attack, stop the extraction and block the attacker.
detail: LALIGA says its security teams identified the origin of the access, but it has not said what that was. Reuters says LALIGA became aware of the attack on Nov 16; CD Eldense's statement, as reported by Cadena SER, says LALIGA learned of it on Nov 18 and told the club on Nov 20 (see c010). All of this rests on the company's statement.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The company states it; no outside source has checked the dates or the containment.
notes: Company statement only; the outlets relay it.

claim_text: LALIGA says the incident was limited to this platform and the competition was not affected
summary: LALIGA says the incident was limited to this one platform and did not affect the rest of its systems or the running of the competition.
detail: This is the company's own finding. The statement says the platform activity is still being analysed to determine the scope.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The company states it; no outside source has checked it.
notes: Company statement only. The CNA copy does not repeat this line.

claim_text: LALIGA says it told the data protection agency and filed a police complaint
summary: LALIGA says it notified Spain's data protection agency (AEPD), filed a complaint with the National Police's cybercrime unit, which is investigating, and told the clubs. Several clubs say they notified the AEPD too.
detail: Getafe CF says it filed its own police complaint. No statement from the agency or the police was found. The notifications rest on LALIGA's and the clubs' own statements.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: LALIGA and the clubs say they made the notifications; no agency or police statement was found.

claim_text: How many people were affected and which data
summary: No count of affected users has been published. Clubs say that, per LALIGA, the data are identifying and contact details (see c009); LALIGA's own statement says only 'personal data'.
detail: Reuters says the extent is yet to be determined. The Record says LALIGA has not disclosed how many fans were affected.
label: Not established

claim_text: Who was behind it and how they got in
summary: LALIGA calls the attacker a 'cibercriminal' and says it identified the origin of the access, but has not said what that was or named anyone. The Record says no group has been linked and ransomware is unclear.
detail: We did not look at leak sites, forums or trackers. Which platform was hit is not named either.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: None of the sources names an attacker or a method; The Record says no group has been linked.

claim_text: Several clubs say their fans are among those whose data was taken
summary: At least six clubs say their fans are among those affected: Getafe CF, Real Oviedo, Girona FC and Albacete Balompié in their own statements, and CD Eldense and Córdoba CF as reported by press.
detail: Each club says its own systems were not affected; the platform is run by LALIGA. Marca also lists Huesca, Tenerife and Cultural Leonesa from their statements; we have not read those. The Record lists Real Zaragoza as affected, but Real Zaragoza's own statement says only that its own systems and member area were not affected and that it notified the AEPD; it does not say whether its fans are among those affected. The Record says Real Madrid and FC Barcelona have not said either way.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Four clubs' own official statements say their users are among those affected.

claim_text: Clubs say, per LALIGA, the data are identifying and contact details, not passwords or bank data
summary: Clubs passing on what LALIGA told them say the data taken are identifying and contact details given when fans registered, and that passwords, bank details and payment data were not compromised, based on what is known so far.
detail: Albacete Balompié says not all of the data was taken for every person. Real Zaragoza says the data do not include login credentials or bank details. LALIGA itself has not published a list of data types.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The clubs state it, but say it comes from LALIGA and is provisional; no independent check.
notes: LALIGA's assessment relayed by the clubs.

claim_text: CD Eldense says LALIGA learned of the incident on Nov 18 and told the club on Nov 20
summary: CD Eldense's statement, as reported by Cadena SER, says LALIGA learned of the incident on Nov 18 and told the club on Nov 20. Reuters says LALIGA became aware on Nov 16, the day it says it blocked the attacker.
detail: The two dates do not match, and LALIGA's own statement gives neither.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One press report of the club's statement gives these dates; LALIGA has not confirmed them.
